title: Qualcomm Lays Off Hundreds and Raises $4B in AI Pivot
summary: Qualcomm is laying off 520 in California and a reported 1,500 in India while raising $4 billion to fund its AI data center pivot. What it means for engineers.

Qualcomm Restructuring


# Qualcomm Lays Off Hundreds and Raises $4B in AI Pivot


By OpenTools Team


·


November 20, 2026


Qualcomm is laying off roughly 520 employees in California and a reported 1,500 in India while raising $4 billion in debt, part of a pivot away from its shrinking smartphone‑chip business toward AI data centers and automotive. CEO Cristiano Amon called the cuts a 'performance‑focused reduction,' but nearly half of layoff discussions on Blind cited favouritism.


## 520 California Cuts, 1,500 Reported in India


Qualcomm is executing a major global restructuring with permanent layoffs of hundreds of employees across California and approximately 1,500 in India, while simultaneously raising $4 billion in debt, according to[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) . The California WARN notices detail about 442 cuts in San Diego — including at its Morehouse Drive headquarters — and roughly 78 in Santa Clara and San Jose, for a total of about 520.


The roles affected are not limited to entry-level staff: senior and principal engineers, engineering directors, vice presidents, and senior directors of technology and product management are all in scope. Individual notices went out November 10–11, with employment ending January 12.


## 'Performance-Focused' on Paper, Favouritism Claims in Practice


CEO Cristiano Amon framed the reductions as a "performance-focused reduction" in an internal memo obtained by[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/qualcomm-cut-jobs-worldwide-performance-focused-layoffs-internal-memo-shows-2026-10-20/) , writing that "we must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can[continue](https://opentools.ai/tools/continue) to succeed."


But employees are pushing back on that framing. According to Blind's internal AI analysis shared with[People Matters](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/qualcomm-india-layoffs-477percent-of-employees-question-managerial-bias-in-job-cuts-53403) , 47.7% of layoff-related discussions about Qualcomm cited politics or favouritism as a factor — higher than the figures for[Meta](https://opentools.ai/organizations/meta) (28.6%),[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) (28%) and Uber (21.1%) during their own peak layoff periods.


## The $4 Billion Debt Raise and $332 Million in Restructuring Costs


The restructuring comes with a price tag. Qualcomm recorded **$332 million** in restructuring and severance costs in its fiscal 2026 annual report, up from just $39 million the prior year, per[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) .[Calcalistech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/8x75ackbs) reported the charges were more than eight times the prior year's figure.


The $4 billion bond offering, disclosed in a November 13 SEC filing, spans five series of notes maturing from 2028 to 2036. Roughly $2 billion will repay debt maturing in May 2027, with the rest going to general corporate purposes and potential acquisitions.


## The Smartphone Business Is Shrinking


The layoffs track a business in decline. Qualcomm's total annual revenue fell 3% to $43.1 billion in fiscal 2026, with Q4 handset-chip revenue down 26% to $5.14 billion, per[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) . Two customer shifts are biting: Apple is transitioning to internally developed modem chips, and Samsung is using Exynos processors in some Galaxy S26 models while keeping Snapdragon in others.


The contrast is stark. Competitor MediaTek grew smartphone-processor revenue 18.3% year over year in Q3 2026, and[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) 's revenue rose 103% to $115.8 billion, per[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) .


## The Bet on AI Data Centers and Automotive


Where Qualcomm is cutting legacy roles, it's betting on growth. The company projects data-center revenue will reach **$5 billion** in fiscal 2027, and automotive revenue grew 89% in Q4 to $1.99 billion, per[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) . The pivot mirrors the broader industry:[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/chipmaker-qualcomm-lays-off-442-021750254.html) noted the chipmaker is expanding into AI data centers even as it sheds smartphone-related roles.


## What It Means for Engineers


The workforce paradox is telling: Qualcomm's global headcount actually grew during fiscal 2026, from about 52,000 to roughly 57,000, even as specific roles were cut, per[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) . For engineers, the signal is clear — AI, data-center and automotive skills are being hired for, while legacy smartphone-chip expertise is being pruned.


Severance in India reportedly includes two months' notice pay plus one month's salary per year of service and a year of continued insurance, per[TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/employment/qualcomm-lays-off-100s-amid-global-restructuring-raises-4-billion) . But the gap between the official "performance-focused" rationale and employees' accounts of favouritism will shape how the layoffs are remembered.
